attack_analysis.human_readable_explanation:
Untrusted input is passed directly into eval(), which executes it as code.
An attacker can inject their own Python instructions to run on the server.
This can lead to system takeover, data theft, or unauthorized access.
Avoid eval() with user input and use safe parsing instead.
attack_analysis.impact: Attacker may execute arbitrary system commands.

attack_analysis.human_readable_explanation:
User input is executed directly as a system command.
Attackers can append their own shell commands to run on the host.
This may lead to server compromise or data theft.
Avoid shell execution or strictly validate and escape inputs.
attack_analysis.impact: Attacker may execute system commands on the host.

attack_analysis.human_readable_explanation:
A real password is stored directly in the source code.
If the repository is leaked or shared, attackers can read it easily.
Those credentials can then be used to access protected systems.
Store secrets in environment variables or a secret manager instead.
attack_analysis.impact: Attacker may gain unauthorized access using exposed credentials.

attack_analysis.human_readable_explanation:
User input is directly concatenated into an SQL query.
Attackers can inject their own SQL to change the query logic.
This can expose private data or allow data modification.
Use parameterized queries or ORM bindings to prevent injection.
attack_analysis.impact: Attacker may read or modify sensitive database records.

attack_analysis.human_readable_explanation:
The code runs subprocesses with shell=True while using external input.
This allows attackers to inject extra shell commands.
Those commands run with the application's permissions.
Disable shell execution and pass arguments safely as a list.
attack_analysis.impact: Attacker may execute arbitrary commands via shell invocation.
